name: The par force hunting landscape in North Zealand
description: Just north of Copenhagen, three royal forests (Store Dyrehave, Gribskov and Jægersborg Dyrehave) were reshaped by Danish kings for hunting with hounds. Straight lanes radiate from central points like stars across a grid, marked by numbered stone posts, so riders could pursue stags through woodland. Walking or cycling these avenues, you can still trace the Baroque geometry, and a royal hunting lodge survives.
